meanings.note: Contrast. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.
Starting a question: а жвачку?. Core Russian conj meaning 'and, but; so' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you.
And where's the toy car?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Бросать трубку = to hang up. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to throw; to abandon', paired with 'бросить'.
Бросать трубку = to hang up. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to throw; to abandon', paired with 'бросить'.

examples.trans: Don't hang up!

examples.text: Он всегда бросает вещи на пол.
examples.trans: He always throws things on the floor.

examples.text: Не бросайте трубку, умоляю вас! Я перед вами стою на коленях.
examples.trans: Don't hang up, I'm begging you! I'm on my knees in front of you.

meanings.note: Polite (вы) or plural. Core Russian det meaning 'your, yours (polite or plural)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Who are your rivals?
Is this your programme?
Arkady Borisovich, who are your rivals?

meanings.note: Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.
Drawing attention. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to see', paired with 'увидеть'.

examples.trans: See?
I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.note: выбирать слова = to choose one's words

examples.trans: He takes a long time choosing a new dish.
Always choose the right words.

examples.text: Выбирай слова, когда говоришь с ней!
examples.trans: Choose your words when talking with her!

meanings.note: + genitive. Core Russian prep meaning 'for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.
This is for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: Currency unit. Common masculine noun meaning 'dollar' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: It costs ten thousand dollars!
The ticket costs a hundred dollars.

examples.text: Возьмите! Они десять тысяч долларов стоят!
examples.trans: Take it! It costs ten thousand dollars!

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.
Dad and Mum.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: joins a description to a noun; agrees with that noun in gender and number

examples.trans: This is a mayor who keeps his word.
Where is the book that was here?

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'someone', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Кто-то не оценил твой отличный ход?
examples.trans: Did someone not appreciate your great move?
Finally someone is for the people!

examples.text: Слушай, тут пишут: «Гордость России! Наконец-то кто-то за народ!»
examples.trans: Listen, here they write: 'Pride of Russia! Finally someone is for the people!'

meanings.note: For movement; где is for location. Core Russian adv meaning 'where (to)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Where are you going?
And where are you going?
Wait, where are you two going?

meanings.note: on a phone or in a restaurant; indeclinable

examples.trans: What's this menu here?
The menu, please.

examples.text: Что за меню здесь? Как позвонить?
examples.trans: What's this menu here? How do I make a call?

meanings.note: + prepositional: на сайте. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.
+ accusative: на второй срок. Core Russian prep meaning 'on, onto; for' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: To a job or a doctor. Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'referral slip; direction' in everyday Russian.
Verbal action/result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание'. Common neuter noun meaning 'referral slip; direction' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: I'll write out a referral right now.
Which direction should we walk in?

examples.text: Сейчас выпишу направление. Где я вас могла видеть?
examples.trans: I'll write out a referral right now. Where could I have seen you?

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

examples.trans: I don't know.
There wasn't enough money.
Chef, I didn't take it.

meanings.note: Negative prefix 'не-' ('un-, non-, not') (stem 'известно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: Without knowing yet where it will lead.

examples.text: На кухне все стараются работать неизвестно.
examples.trans: In the kitchen everyone tries to work unknown.

meanings.note: Descriptive Russian adjective meaning 'some', agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies.

examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a chance.
Some guests ordered dessert.

examples.text: Некоторым сама жизнь даёт второй шанс.
examples.trans: To some, life itself gives a second chance.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian personal or demonstrative pronoun meaning 'nobody', inherited from Common Slavic roots and used constantly in natural spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Никто не будет командовать на моей кухне!
examples.trans: Nobody is going to give orders in my kitchen!

examples.text: Не говори об этом никому, ладно?
examples.trans: Do not tell anyone about this, okay?
But legally you are nobody to her.

meanings.note: Stronger contrast than 'а'. Core Russian conj meaning 'but' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

оказаться.gloss: to turn out to be, find oneself

meanings.en: to turn out to be, prove to be
meanings.note: Reflexive verb. Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to turn out to be, find oneself', paired with 'оказываться'.

examples.trans: You turned out to be ungrateful.

examples.text: Он внезапно оказался в центре событий.
examples.trans: He suddenly found himself in the center of events.
And you turned out to be an ungrateful woman!

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('okay') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: А я пойду принесу выпить, окей?
examples.trans: I will go grab us something to drink, okay?

examples.text: Я уже всё решил. Одну треть на кладбище, две трети над океаном.
examples.trans: I've already sorted it all out. One third goes to the cemetery, two thirds over the ocean.

передать.gloss: to pass on, to hand over

meanings.en: to pass on, to hand over, to give
meanings.note: + accusative and dative (кому). Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'дать'). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to pass on, to hand over', paired with 'передавать'.

examples.trans: Give this to Alexei.
Please pass on my regards to your mum.

examples.text: Всё, я ухожу. Ребёнок ни при чём. Передай это Алексею.
examples.trans: That's it, I'm leaving. The child isn't to blame. Give this to Alexei.

meanings.note: Common neuter noun meaning 'crossroads' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: А кто-то, оказавшись на перепуте, выбирает направление.
examples.trans: While someone else, standing at a crossroads, chooses a direction.

examples.text: На нашей кухне уже есть новое перепутье.
examples.trans: In our kitchen there is already a new crossroads.

meanings.note: Подавать на развод. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to serve, submit, file'.
Food or items. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to serve, submit, file'.

examples.text: Как будто ты подаёшь на развод.
examples.trans: As if you are filing for divorce.

examples.text: Подавай мясо на горячей тарелке гостям.
examples.trans: Serve the meat to the guests on a hot plate.

examples.text: Вика, скорее подавай гостям горячие блюда!
examples.trans: Vika, serve the hot dishes to the guests quickly!

meanings.note: Handing something over.
Answer to thanks.
Handing something over.

examples.trans: A coffee, please.
Thank you! — You're welcome.
Please see him out.

meanings.note: Informal. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.
As an adverb. Core Russian interj meaning 'bye' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Bye!
Bye, Dad!
Bye, darling!

meanings.note: Полный кошмар = a total nightmare. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').
Полный кошмар = a total nightmare. Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('full, complete, total').

examples.trans: This is a total nightmare!

examples.text: На столе стоял полный стакан воды.
examples.trans: A full glass of water stood on the table.

examples.text: Ну что я тебе скажу, Аркаша? Это полный кошмар!
examples.trans: Well, what can I tell you, Arkasha? This is a total nightmare!

meanings.note: from a trip, by car, train or plane

examples.trans: Dad brought presents.
What did you bring?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Verbal action or result neuter noun formed with '-ение'/'-ание', meaning 'adventure' in conversational and formal Russian.

examples.trans: The main adventure is only just beginning!

examples.text: В Москве Макса ждали новые приключения.
examples.trans: New adventures awaited Max in Moscow.

examples.text: И главное приключение ещё только начинается!
examples.trans: And the main adventure is only just beginning!

meanings.note: + 3rd person verb: 'пусть строят' = let them build

examples.trans: Let them build.
Let him come.

examples.text: Ты преподавай. А они пусть строят свои торговые центры.
examples.trans: You teach. And let them build their shopping centres.

meanings.note: Arduous path. Common masculine noun meaning 'path, way, journey' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: Here is a movie: A Thorny Path.

examples.text: Давай, счастливого пути и хорошей дороги!
examples.trans: Go ahead, safe travels and have a good road!

examples.text: Ты сам выбрал этот страшный путь.
examples.trans: You chose this terrible path yourself.

meanings.note: + genitive plural: пятьсот рублей. Core Russian num meaning 'five hundred' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: It costs five hundred roubles.
About five hundred roubles.

examples.text: Пятьсот. А у меня ни копейки.
examples.trans: Five hundred. And I haven't got a penny.

meanings.note: The Russian currency. Common masculine noun meaning 'rouble' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: This costs a hundred roubles.
I haven't got a single rouble.

examples.text: Наша задача — взять у взяточников миллиард рублей.
examples.trans: Our task is to take a billion roubles from the bribe-takers.

meanings.note: pan with a handle used for frying food

examples.trans: A heavy frying pan was sizzling on the stove.

examples.text: Он быстро снял сковородку с огня.
examples.trans: He quickly took the frying pan off the heat.

examples.text: Во имя тяжёлой сковородки и половника!
examples.trans: In the name of the heavy frying pan and ladle!

meanings.note: сто пятьдесят = a hundred and fifty; сто рублей = a hundred roubles

examples.trans: I need a hundred roubles.
I've got a hundred and ten.

examples.text: Понимаешь, Аркаша, мы все скидываемся на этот кластер. Мне москвичам сегодня надо отдать сто пятьдесят.
examples.trans: You see, Arkasha, we're all chipping in for this cluster. I have to give the Moscow people a hundred and fifty today.

meanings.note: Derived masculine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'small table'.

examples.text: Они заняли свободный столик у окна.
examples.trans: They took a free table near the window.
Would you like to sit at an available table?
To a guest at the next table.

meanings.note: Hot liquid dish. Borrowed from French 'soupe' in the Petrine era.

examples.text: Сегодня на кухне сварили вкусный суп.
examples.trans: Today in the kitchen they cooked delicious soup.
I like hot soup very much!

examples.text: Мы добавим таблетку в её суп?
examples.trans: Shall we add the pill into her soup?

meanings.note: One person, informal. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

meanings.en: other forms: тебя (gen/acc), тебе (dat), тобой (instr), тебе (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'you (informal)' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: You're greedy!
Have you got any more?
Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.trans: That means thousands of jobs.
A thousand roubles.

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

увидеться.gloss: to see each other, meet up

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'видеться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as a perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to see each other, meet up', paired with 'видеться'.

examples.text: Послушай, мы сегодня увидимся вечером с тобой?
examples.trans: Listen, will we see each other this evening?
See you tomorrow!
All right, see you in the kitchen, administrator!

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'держаться'). Used in Russian as a perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to resist'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.text: Я не удержалась и купила пёсика.
examples.trans: I could not resist and bought a puppy.

examples.text: Я просто не удержалась и купила этого милого пёсика.
examples.trans: I simply could not resist and bought this cute little dog.

examples.text: Трудно удержаться от улыбки, когда Луи начинает петь.
examples.trans: It is hard to hold back a smile when Louis starts singing.

успевать.gloss: to manage in time, have time

meanings.en: to manage in time, have enough time
meanings.note: Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to manage in time'.

examples.trans: We cannot get anything done in time.

examples.text: Повара ничего не успевают вовремя отдавать.
examples.trans: The cooks cannot serve anything on time.

examples.text: Я не успеваю. Это в другую сторону.
examples.trans: I do not have time. That is the other way.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('turtle, tortoiseshell').

examples.text: Понимаете, у нас нет в меню черепахового супа.
examples.trans: You see, we do not have turtle soup on our menu.

examples.text: Передайте шеф-повару, пусть подает черепаховый суп, окей?
examples.trans: Tell the head chef to serve the turtle soup, okay?

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Conjunction. Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.
Core Russian pron meaning 'what' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: What's this?
Look what I've got.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.
examples.trans: Hi! Look what I've got.

meanings.note: Declinable neuter noun meaning 'miracle', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: This is a culinary miracle!

examples.text: Потому что это настоящее кулинарное чудо!
examples.trans: Because it is a real culinary miracle!
Just wait for a miracle.

meanings.note: chief cook in a professional kitchen

examples.trans: The head chef manages the entire kitchen.

examples.text: Они привели нового шеф-повара прямо из Индии.
examples.trans: They brought a new chef straight from India.

examples.text: Шеф-повар решит, подходите ли вы ресторану.
examples.trans: The head chef will decide whether you suit the restaurant.

meanings.note: alone: 'я этого не хочу' = I don't want that

examples.trans: This house.
I'm sick of this communal flat.

examples.text: Меня уже тошнит от этой коммуналки! У нас труба уже неделю течёт.
examples.trans: I'm sick of this communal flat! Our pipe has been leaking for a week now.
